landing_intro: Co-planning brings general and special educators together to plan instruction as a team, so students who learn differently still get full access to grade-level content. These resources cover how to set it up, protect the time, run strong planning sessions, and use the structures that make it stick.

Repeated reading builds reading fluency through short, structured, repeated practice. These resources give you the protocol, the scheduling and grouping guidance, and the tools to run it well across tiers, whether in a small group or a whole class.

A routine data cycle is a regular rhythm for collecting student data, reading it together, and adjusting instruction. These resources walk through each step, from setting the conditions, to running the cycle, to planning from what the data shows.

Strong practices need strong implementation. This section is for the leaders putting these practices in place: how to onboard teams, coach the work, track progress, and sustain it past the first year. It pulls together the playbooks, agendas, and tools that make adoption stick.

The people and schools behind the practices. Spotlights on partners in the IGNITE Network, case studies of schools putting the work in place, and talks from the field — the story of what is being built and learned together.

How the Research-to-Impact practices are working, and the difference they make for students. White papers, the external evaluation, annual reports, and the roadmap for closing the equity gap. Written for leaders, partners, and funders.

Beyond the featured toolkits, Marshall's Research-to-Impact library holds a broader set of practices developed with schools, across literacy, collaboration, data use, postsecondary readiness, and student support. These move onto the site over time.
